note:
201/9's ABLATION SWEEP, TAKEN IN FULL: seven arms on the phone. There is no `timestamp-query` on this adapter and no browser flag brings it, so a pass is priced by REMOVING it and re-flying the route (201/9-00): each arm is a page carrying one `?ablate=` (or `?bloomlevels=`), flown over the SAME ten-leg route inside the pak's own rect, and its window is the DELTA of two `frame.dtHistogramMs` readings — one after the four corners were warmed and the camera had settled at the centre pose, one after the last leg. `moving` is every bin below the 100 ms tail (the render gate's idle wake). READ THE MEAN, not p50: p50 saturates on the 16.7 ms vsync floor. MGA-LX3 / ARM Bifrost @ DPR 2, pak `19:23 28-08-2026` ASTC over `los-santos-centre`, app `5937214+`, board EMPTY (`units=0&calls=0`), `?surface=720x640` pinning the drawing buffer on every arm. Every arm's `surface.ablated` was read back before its numbers were kept.

THE BASELINE IS ALSO A CONTROL, and it had to be. The session before this one flew its ladder through an agent link that could hand the camera an incomplete pose; a pose missing its heading gave a NaN eye, which draws BLACK — and a black frame is a CHEAP frame, so a window flown through one reads as fast rather than as broken. Nothing recorded said whether the 09-04 ladder had been flown that way. So the first arm here is `field` on the FIXED app over the identical route: moving mean 23.4 ms against the 09-04 ladder's 24.5, p50 20 against 20, 29 cell creates in the window against 29. The two agree, so THE 09-04 LADDER STANDS and its conclusions are not withdrawn.

WHAT THE SWEEP SAYS, and it settles 201/9-05 by refuting the shape the step assumed.

  arm       what it removes                       moving frames   mean     delta    p95   rung 1
  field     nothing (the baseline)                      416      23.4 ms      -       38    59 %
  nobloom   the whole bloom chain                       614      15.8 ms   -7.7 ms    18    99 %
  nocells   every resident cell's bundles               501      19.6 ms   -3.8 ms    32    79 %
  nocloud   the per-frame 256^2 cumulus bake            454      21.6 ms   -1.8 ms    38    67 %
  noprobe   what PROBE_FRAME_INTERVAL leaves            449      21.9 ms   -1.6 ms    38    65 %
  noskylut  what the LUT's own input key leaves         438      22.5 ms   -1.0 ms    38    61 %
  bloom4    the chain's TAIL (8 levels -> 4)            437      23.2 ms   -0.2 ms    40    59 %

THE BLOOM CHAIN IS 7.7 ms OF A 23.4 ms FRAME — a third of it — and removing it is the only change measured on this device that reaches the declared 60 fps: 607 of 614 frames on ONE display interval, p95 18 ms against 38. AND THE TAIL IS FREE. `bloom4` cuts the chain from 8 levels to 4 — every level 201/9-05 named as waste, the ones that are 12x10, 6x5 and 3x3 pixels at this surface — and costs 23.2 ms, which is the baseline. So the money is in the FIRST levels, the ones at full and half resolution, exactly where the 09-04 ladder's `rgb10a2` arm said it was: the post chain's BANDWIDTH, paid per pixel by the two or three biggest passes, not per pass by the small ones. Deriving the level count from the render size — 9/05 as written — would therefore buy approximately NOTHING, and the step needs re-aiming rather than building.

THE CLOUD BAKE IS 1.8 ms, and unlike the bloom result it is free to take: the field scrolls at `t * 0.004` and is visually identical for minutes, so amortizing it (201/9-06) changes no pixel a person can see. That is the one arm here that converts directly into a fix.

AND THE WORLD IS CHEAPER THAN THE FRAME AROUND IT. `nocells` removes every resident cell's opaque and blend bundles — 96 draws and 242 k triangles, the whole reason this surface exists — for 3.8 ms, HALF what the bloom chain costs. The scene pass still clears and resolves with it off, so what this prices is the geometry alone; read together with `nobloom` it says the per-pixel work of the post chain outweighs the per-triangle work of the city by two to one at this pose. Whatever is spent making the map show more world is spent against a frame whose largest single item is not the world.

THE TWO ALREADY-AMORTIZED BAKES STILL COST. `noprobe` is 1.6 ms and `noskylut` 1.0 — of passes that are supposed to be nearly free, one amortized over `PROBE_FRAME_INTERVAL` and one short-circuited by its own input key. They bound what is left in each rather than naming a fix, and together they are 2.6 ms: more than the cumulus bake this chain opened on. Neither is a lever yet; both are worth a second look at what actually runs on a frame that should skip them.

THE FIRST FOUR ARMS COST TWO ATTEMPTS. Switching arms opened a SECOND console tab twice (the panel steered an ATTACHED page and launched when it was not, and Android detaches a backgrounded tab after 15 s); two consoles sharing one GPU is not a measurement. `surface.ablated` and the readout's pose caught both, and those runs were discarded rather than filed. The last three arms were taken after the opener learned to steer a sleeping tab.

THE SUM DOES NOT CLOSE, and that is expected. The five named removals add to 15.9 ms of a 23.4 ms frame; the remainder is what no arm here can remove — the scene pass's own clear and resolve, the post pass, the composite, and the vsync quantization every mean is read through. An ablation prices a GROUP by its absence and never accounts for a whole frame.

AND NO ROW HERE RECORDS THE BATTERY OR THE CHARGING STATE, this one included. It stays an open debt against every mobile row in this folder.

route.warmup: the rect's four corners, then the settle pose, before the first reading

howDerived: per arm: delta of frame.dtHistogramMs between a post-warmup reading and a post-route reading; moving = every bin below the 100 ms tail (the render gate's idle wake); vsyncLadder = each moving bin rounded to the nearest 1/60 s interval

control.verdict: the 09-04 ladder was not flown through a black frame; its numbers and its conclusions stand
